PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:02 pm

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.7.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,

Jane Fall – I am the Executive Director of Our Saviour Center a social services non-
profit outreach organization. I am here to formerly thank everybody in this body and
everybody who has supported our organization over the years. I specifically wanted to
thank you all for your continued support of our Soccer for Success program which is a
program that has been in existence about ten years and during the last five years the
City has been one of our significant partners in the process. I will invite you all to one of
our twelve Saturdays coming up starting on the 29th where about 500 to 700 children are
playing soccer between 8:00 am and noon. These games are meant to help the children
improve their health and their cardio and physical abilities. Part of our program is to help
them understand the importance of eating healthier and eating good nutritious food. That
is part of the program that happens twice a week we have instructors go out to the
different school sites and the children are able to participate this is K through the 10th
grade. I also want to let you know that the financial support that this body helps provide
provides all of these services to the children for free. The get shin guards, soccer balls
and a team jersey, healthy snacks and all of the instructions are paid through the
financial support. We thank you for that we feel that this is a wonderful program for our
community. I also just wanted to let you know that one of the lovely aspects of this
program is that it provides a career path, work experience and also the possibility to give
back by the instructors. Many of our instructors who are trained come to us out of our
direct community El Monte.

Charles Hoffman – Tonight I am here as a Director for the El Monte Historical Society to
invite one and all to our tea on Sunday the 23rd it is this Sunday from 1:00 pm to 3:00 pm
open to all. It will be hosted by our Board of Directors and that is at 3150 Tyler Avenue,
El Monte. I would also like to say this is 2020 the year of the Census please be counted.

Gabriel Ramirez – I want to address one issue that is happening on my block on Valley
and Gibson I believe I have been addressing this for quite a while. I believe I spoke
about it and used the GoRequest app it is the lighting signal on Valley and Gibson is
very confusing when you make a turn. It does not have a signal for a left turn or right
turn and it is very confusing to the point where you don’t know if when you make a turn
you have to wait your turn because cars are speeding. A couple of years if you may
know there was an accident of someone who got run over and I know I brought it up
before. I know it was the past Public Works Director and the past City Managers and it
was well know so I just want you to know for the staff to really look and see if there is an
option where we can have a traffic study properly done and also having a signal there for
a left turn because it is a very confusing. Lastly at the last meeting I wasn’t there but I
was very surprised that Councilmember Velasco voted against no and that was the first
time that I see in the vote but keep it up thank you.

Cosme Jimenez – I couldn’t make it to the last meeting but I would like to congratulate
Councilmember Velasco for voting no at the last meeting that really meant a lot because
you voted no you surprised me and everybody and that is the way it is supposed to be.
That was an item related to not enough parking spaces. Developers have been building
and continue to build in this City and getting away with not enough parking spaces.
Even Ex-Councilmember Gomez always voted no not enough parking spaces 1.5 cars
per house or condominium is ridiculous. When Councilmember Velasco first started the
Council seat promised that he was going to follow the footsteps of Ex-Councilmember
Patel and represent the community first that was the first two months but never
continued. Something happened at the last meeting and that is why I am saying this we
have been waiting for the representation of the people all the time not just once in a
while.

Stephen Trumble – I am here from the Norwood Library on Peck Road up on the
northern part of the City and I am here to announce a few programs they are all
happening on the same day incredibly enough. This Saturday the 22nd we are having a
decluttering program at 11:00 am. While all of this is going on at our library we have in
our meeting room Vita Tax Prep Volunteers form 10:00 am to 4:00 pm. I also want to let
you know that the Vita Tax Prep people will be at the El Monte Library on Tyler Avenue
on Saturday, March 14th from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm and at the Baldwin Park Library on
Saturday March 21st and Saturday, April 11th from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm. Now the
volunteer tax assistance consist of IRS certified volunteers and they usually help people
who make $55,000 or less, people with disabilities, or limited English they help them do
their taxes. On Tuesday, February 25th at 6:00 pm in the Norwood Library we will have
